study type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
exposure: soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 to placental growth factor ratio (sFlt-1/PlGF ratio) at 36 weeks' gestation
outcome: Interval to spontaneous onset of labor
Intrapartum fetal compromise requiring cesarean delivery
cohort: 23,831 women with singleton, low-risk pregnancies who had spontaneous onset of labor after routine assessment at 35+0 to 36+6 weeks' gestation.
finding: An increased sFlt-1/PlGF ratio at 36 weeks' gestation is associated with an earlier gestational age at spontaneous onset of labor and higher rates of intrapartum fetal compromise.
mod_finding: An increased sFlt-1/PlGF ratio at 36 weeks' gestation increases the risk for intrapartum fetal compromise that requires cesarean delivery.
gest_age: Measurement taken at 35+0 to 36+6 weeks' gestation; spontaneous onset of labor occurred at mean 39.2 weeks' gestation for high ratio group vs 40.0 weeks' gestation for low ratio group.
